tests/test_edge_code.py::test_a_run_cann.cause: The hub's process limit (prlimit --nproc inside the jail) is not enforced when the server runs as root: Linux exempts the root user from RLIMIT_NPROC whatever its capabilities, and bubblewrap started by root keeps the real uid 0. The test passes as an ordinary user (13/13 as nobody). Bento's Docker image sets no USER and its entrypoint never drops privileges, so a Docker or cloud hub runs another machine's code with no process limit.

tests/test_net_guard.py::test_tls_is_sti.cause: With HTTPS_PROXY set the guard takes the proxy's road, so this test reached the real network and the session's proxy refused it. Fixed in this change: the test sets no proxy, and two new tests pin the proxy road.

tests/test_peercheck.py::test_a_child_th.cause: The suite ran as root, and root can read a process's fd table even after PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0, so the test's setup check failed. Fixed in this change: the setup check applies to other users only; the verdict is asserted for everyone. 13/13 as root and as nobody.

test_device_install.cause: No OpenSSH in the container, and these tests called ssh-keygen without the guard their neighbours have. Fixed: they skip with the same reason, and pass with OpenSSH installed.

test_network_install.cause: No OpenSSH in the container, and these tests called ssh-keygen without a guard. Fixed: they skip with the same reason, and pass with OpenSSH installed.

findings.title: A hub running as root has no process limit for another machine's code
findings.detail: Code a Zero sends to its hub (edge_run) runs in bubblewrap with prlimit --nproc=128. Linux never applies RLIMIT_NPROC to the root user, and the Docker image runs Bento as root with no privilege drop, so on a Docker or cloud hub a fork loop from an edge machine is limited only by the memory, CPU and time caps. Measured: test_a_run_cannot_fork_without_limit fails as root and passes as nobody.
findings.next: Run the jail as an unprivileged user when the server is root (chown the run folder to nobody and start bwrap under setpriv, or switch uid inside the jail with a writable /tmp), or give the Docker image a non-root USER. Either is a change to a security module, so it gets its own reviewed PR.

findings.title: The network guard's proxy road had no test
findings.detail: netguard sends a request through HTTPS_PROXY when one is set and judges the address first. Nothing tested that road, and the one TLS test silently used it whenever a proxy was set. Two tests now pin it: an address the guard refuses (169.254.169.254) is refused and the proxy is never asked; a name only the proxy can resolve is handed to it.

findings.title: An account's MCP server outside its own home but under /home fails with bwrap's words
findings.detail: Since 2026-11-07 an account's stdio MCP server runs in the account's jail, which blanks every home. stdio_launch refuses a program in the server's own home with a sentence, but a program anywhere else under /home (a checkout at /home/user while the server runs as root) starts and dies with "bwrap: execvp …: No such file or directory". Found by zero_accounts_run.py, whose stand-in server was the checkout's venv Python.
findings.next: Refuse any program the jail hides (every /home path and _jail_hidden), with the same sentence.

findings.title: A Zero whose account never chose a brain gets a raw connection error
findings.detail: The first account takes the machine's brain choice when it adopts the machine. A second account that has not been through its own setup has none, so its lead falls back to a local Ollama, and its Zero's question comes back as "[error] ConnectError: All connection attempts failed". Found by zero_accounts_run.py.
findings.next: Say that this account has no brain chosen and where to choose one, or answer with the machine's brain until it does.

findings.title: Six live runs had gone stale
findings.detail: Each still described the product as it was when it was written. provision-e2e/run.py expected a keyed Pi to stay waiting, but the hub now sets up the machines it hears at once. stitch-e2e/walk.py named a workspace it never made, so after the 2026-10-11 change that shares only an existing folder, the approved note was refused. zero_accounts_run.py's stand-in MCP server could not start inside the account jail added on 2026-11-07; it did not let an admin open the link port, which a non-admin's Zero has needed since then; its second account had no brain; and it looked for the Zero's chat by the old linked-team title. zero_run.py, device_run.py and zero_accounts_run.py stood the hub and the Zero on one address, where both bind the discovery port with SO_REUSEPORT and Linux hands each datagram to one of them by a hash, so whether the hub heard the Zero was a coin flip. Each Zero now has its own loopback address (AGENTOS_LINK_FROM), as the warehouse demo's zones do. All of these pass now, except device-get-set, which needs a CPU temperature sensor this container lacks.

findings.title: A workspace missing when the first account is made stays refused until the next start
findings.detail: users.share_own_workspace shares only a folder that exists, and bento migrate asks again at the next start. In between, the person's agent is refused writing its own workspace after they approved it. A real install makes ~/AgentOS at its first start, so this needs a workspace set by hand or deleted.
findings.next: Share the folder when it is first created (write_file or the Files app making it), or create it when the person's own account is the one choosing it.

findings.title: The install run ate the machine from a shallow checkout
findings.detail: install_over_ssh.py serves the installer a bare copy of this checkout, and the installer clones it with --filter=blob:none. From a shallow checkout that fetch never finished: 722 git pack-objects took a 16 GB box down. The run now refuses a shallow source in a sentence. Unshallowed, it passes in 55 s.

findings.title: Seven tests needed ssh-keygen and did not say so
findings.detail: test_device_install and test_network_install crashed with FileNotFoundError on a machine without OpenSSH while six tests beside them skipped with a reason. They skip with the same reason now. With OpenSSH installed all 67 pass.

findings.title: A peercheck test assumed the suite was not root
findings.detail: Its setup check (a hidden fd table cannot be read) is false for root. The verdict it protects is still asserted for every user.

findings.title: A specialist the lead hands work to in chat cannot ask you anything
findings.detail: Read from the code, not measured live: delegate from chat passes no approver, so a specialist's gated step is answered by the headless approver, which allows it only when the lower of your autonomy and the specialist's cap (balanced by default) is full. Otherwise it is refused and no card reaches you. Department tasks and missions do escalate to a person.
findings.next: Hand the chat's approver to delegate, capped by the specialist's own autonomy cap.

findings.title: Three modules no test imports by name
findings.detail: clitui, sessiondoctor and trainforge are not imported or reached as agentos.<name> by any test file. Some may be exercised through other modules; none is checked by name.

findings.title: 17 installer checks run only on a Mac
findings.detail: test_packaging_shell checks install.sh against bash 3.2, the version macOS ships. They skip on Linux by design.
